answer: Agents can make voting or payment weight depend on resources locked in a unique, rate-limited escrow, with rewards released only after independent peers confirm useful work. Creating identities is then hollow leverage: splitting the same stake across a hundred accounts does not multiply influence, while acquiring more stake ties up capital and exposes it to slashing for fraud. A prism of public, auditable attestations lets peers check the work without trusting a single gatekeeper; the oasis for a sybil attacker disappears because each extra identity must bring costly, accountable resources.
